title: Random traffic with a burst
question: How much variability comes from randomness alone, and what does a burst do to queues?
description: Three healthy servers, Poisson arrivals and exponential service times. A 10 s burst adds 120 req/s at 30 s. There is no fault: this is the reference for what normal variability looks like. Change only the seed to see a different random outcome.
assumptions: Abstract request-level model: no TCP, TLS, packets or real HTTP proxy semantics.
Each server has fixed concurrency slots and a FIFO queue; there is no CPU, memory or GC model.
Health probes bypass the request queue and answer instantly when the server is up.
Servers do not know when a client gave up; they finish the work and the late response is discarded.
No retries: every failed request is final.
Numbers are scenario inputs, not measured performance of any product.
expectedObservations: Latency varies from request to request even without any failure.
During the burst, queues grow and p95 latency rises; a few requests may be rejected or time out.
Different seeds give slightly different numbers; a single seed is a demonstration, not statistical evidence.
